dedup_decision.count_discrepancy: The REQUEST-LEDGER-2 card (and TVS-REGRADE's headline) say 9 decidable files and 5 legacy files. A direct schema census says 11 and 3: the three files that cannot be decided are rows-baseline, rows-equalinfo and rows-live, all of which carry a second-resolution ts_utc and no content_sha256. The published arithmetic -- 30 excess rows, 1,071 de-duplicated requests -- is identical either way, because every one of the 30 excess rows sits in a decidable file.

rule: one request per row representing an inference call: kind in {turn, tool-followup} count; billed=false, followup_suppressed, served_from=='prompt' do not; a row whose schema cannot decide is counted and flagged assumed_billed

not_exclusion_markers.billed_round: fetch-ROUND accounting; a pinned serve is still a request
not_exclusion_markers.fetch_followup: marks a row that IS a real follow-up request
not_exclusion_markers.is_checkpoint: NOT a billing marker: checkpoint rows are genuine calls

counting.assumed_billed_means: row carries no recognised kind marker; counted because an unmarked row that reached the wire must not vanish from the budget

marker_reconciliation.verdict: implemented exclusion (row says it was not billed); DEAD in this corpus -- 0 rows carry the field, so it can never change the count today

implemented exclusion (client skipped the call); DEAD at row level -- 0 rows carry the field. It occurs only NESTED inside tool_calls[], where the writer records a follow-up the allowance refused; that refusal emitted no row, so a row-level check can never see it

implemented exclusion (served out of the prompt, no call); DEAD at row level -- 0 rows carry the field. `served_from: prompt` occurs NESTED inside tool_calls[], describing the served block of a follow-up that was still bought as a request

reported, never subtracted: writer-emitted, NOT an exclusion: it marks whether a follow-up read fresh lines and so consumed a fetch ROUND. A pinned prompt serve costs no round and is still a request -- the writer's own followups_spent() counts it. False rows stay counted
reported, never subtracted: writer-emitted, NOT an exclusion: it marks a row that IS a real follow-up request (kind=tool-followup). Treating it as suppression would delete 68 real requests
reported, never subtracted: writer-emitted, NOT an exclusion: a per-round cache-accounting counter (0/1/2), not the `served_from` marker. A row with prompt_served=1 still bought a request
